item.title: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
Okay, so… reverted one change due to the sheer number of edits made today, but there was only one fix that potentially counts as problematic so that has been addressed.

As a general note, the applicable (though somewhat obscure) grammar rule regarding the commas seems to be as follows: https://english.stackexchange.com/questions/30516/should-i-use-a-comma-before-and-or-or

When a coordinating conjunction is used to connect a dependent clause, a comma is never used.

However, there is some doubt about it:

In compound predicates, a comma is not usually used, though it may be needed to avoid confusion or indicate a pause. ("She recognized the man who entered the room, and gasped" vs. "She recognized the man who entered the room and gasped.")

So… for this case, it likely would be up to the author to make the final call.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Activity at this stage seems to be initially located in “comfort” and “contentment” centers, with activity shifting into “fear” and “alarm” centers as conversion continues.

SCP-510 absorbs the remaining tissues, including the brain, over a period of 12 to 14 hours. Brain scans show highly elevated levels of activity, consistent with extreme fear or pain at this point, which slowly shift back into a more “relaxed” state as the brain is absorbed.

This was what made the article for me. The fact that the host's contentment and relaxation gives way to horror as they become aware of what is happening to them, and then they experience a final spike in pain and terror before their brain is absorbed and their identity is replaced with plush softness before ceasing to exist altogether.
